title: Stacked guarded levels are not inlined into a 2^k tree
verdict: plan and run stay small at 40 levels
description: Forty stacked projections, each appending a reach and a guarded column that read the previous reach twice (so an optimizer that merges projections by substitution would build a tree of 2^40 copies), plan and run in well under a second of engine time and under 100 MB of extra memory. Optimized plan text by levels (5, 10, 20, 40): 850, 2,017, 5,239 and 11,963 characters (the optimized logical plan); planning 0.25 s to 0.82 s; running 1.7 s to 2.1 s (a local[2] session; most of it is the session's start); process peak including the JVM 723 MB to 821 MB. The plan text grows about linearly. The result matches the reference at every level.
reference: No reference counterpart: the reference has no plan size. D50-d needs the plan of a chain of k guarded levels to cost time and memory linear in k.

evidence.note: `python -m sverify_dev.guarded_columns p2 --engine spark`: PySpark 4.3.0, local[2], ANSI on, Linux x86_64 (homelab); the P1 cases also ran on macOS arm64 for DuckDB and Polars with the same result.

provenance.notes: Issue #1719 (D50-d). Probe rows: 3000, every third one the text `bad`, which a strict cast rejects.
